title: Kids & Family Costs
description: The first year, childcare, two 2026 tax benefits, and a policy once someone depends on you.
wolfLine: The credit is not the childcare bill. Count them apart.

dependent-care-fsa.definition: A work account for childcare or care of a qualifying dependent. In 2026 the federal exclusion is up to $7,500 per household, or $3,750 if you are married filing separately, and only if your plan offers that limit.
dependent-care-fsa.example: Childcare of $9,600. A plan that offers the full 2026 limit can cover $7,500 of it.

child-tax-credit.definition: A federal credit of up to $2,200 per qualifying child for 2026. It starts to shrink above $200,000 of income, or $400,000 if you are married filing jointly.
child-tax-credit.example: Two qualifying children, and income under the 2026 line: up to $2,200 × 2 = $4,400.

529-plan.definition: A savings plan for education. Qualified withdrawals are tax-free at the federal level. The balance can go down, and this course does not promise a return.
529-plan.example: You put in $100 a month. What it is worth later depends on the investments, not on a guaranteed rate.

lessons.title: The First Year
lessons.summary: This page stops before childcare. That bill is its own lesson.

steps.title: Four lines, not the whole story
steps.body:
Gear **$600**. Diapers and wipes **$80** a month, which is **$960**. Formula **$100** a month, which is **$1,200**. Checkup copays **$240**.

The total is **$3,000**, and childcare is not in it.

lessons.title: Childcare
lessons.summary: The monthly tuition is the number that moves the budget.

steps.prompt: What does the center cost in a year?
What does the home day care cost in a year?
How much more is the center per year?
How much more is the center per month?
You need care five days a week and the $400 gap is the whole difference you care about. Which page costs less?
choices: They cost the same per year
steps.explain: Home day care is $9,600. The center is $14,400. Price is not the only reason to choose, but it is the gap on these pages.

lessons.title: The Care Account and the Credit
lessons.summary: Two different 2026 benefits. Do not add them into one bucket.

steps.title: 2026, from the IRS
steps.body:
A [[Dependent Care FSA|dependent-care-fsa]] is a work account. For 2026 the federal exclusion is up to **$7,500** per household, or **$3,750** if you are married filing separately. Your employer has to offer that limit. Many plans used to stop at $5,000.

The [[child tax credit]] is separate. For 2026 it is up to **$2,200** per qualifying child, and it starts to shrink above **$200,000** of income, or **$400,000** if you are married filing jointly. This lesson does not cover the Child and Dependent Care Credit. That is a third thing.

steps.prompt: Childcare is $9,600 and your plan offers the full $7,500. How much childcare is left outside the FSA?
You are married filing separately, so the 2026 FSA limit is $3,750. Childcare is $9,600. How much is outside the FSA?
One qualifying child, and your income is under the 2026 phaseout. What is the child tax credit, at the full amount?
steps.explain: Up to $2,200 for that child. Income under $200,000, or under $400,000 if married filing jointly, is what keeps the full amount in play.

steps.prompt: The $7,500 dependent-care limit and the $2,200 child tax credit are the same benefit counted twice.
steps.explain: One is a work account for care expenses. The other is a tax credit per qualifying child. They are different, and a third credit exists that this lesson does not teach.

lessons.title: A 529 Plan
lessons.summary: Money for school. Not a promised return.

steps.title: Tax-free if you use it for school
steps.body:
A [[529 plan]] is for education. Qualified withdrawals are tax-free at the federal level. The investments inside can fall.

**$100** a month is **$1,200** a year of contributions. That is the part you control. The balance later is not a rate this course will invent.

steps.prompt: You contribute $100 a month. How much is that in a year?
You contribute $100 a month for 5 years. How much have you put in, before any investment change?
What can you say for sure about a 529?
choices: Qualified education withdrawals are tax-free at the federal level
The balance will rise by a set percent every year
The state must match what you put in
steps.explain: The tax treatment of qualified withdrawals is the rule. The return is not.

steps.prompt: A 529 is the same account as a dependent care FSA.
steps.explain: The FSA pays this year’s care, up to the plan limit. A 529 is savings for education later.

steps.title: A small paycheck they can see
steps.body:
A simple sketch is three jars. Spend, save, give.

A **$10** gift becomes **$5** to spend, **$3** to save, and **$2** to give. The amounts matter less than the habit of splitting the money on purpose.

steps.prompt: The gift is $10. Spend $5, save $3, give $2. Do the three jars use the whole gift?
She gets $10 a week and saves $3 each time. How much is in the save jar after 8 weeks?
What is the point of the three jars?
choices: To practice choosing, before the amounts are large
To hide money from the household budget
steps.explain: The habit is the lesson. A 529 can still exist beside it.

steps.prompt: Kids should only see the spend jar, so saving stays an adult topic.
steps.explain: The save jar is how saving becomes visible.

lessons.title: Once Someone Depends on You
lessons.summary: The policy from the protecting section now has a reason.

steps.title: A dependent changes the question
steps.body:
[[Term life insurance|term-life]] pays if you die during the term. The [[beneficiary]] is who receives it.

Before anyone depended on your income, the policy had no job. A child who needs your paycheck is the job. Name the beneficiary on purpose, and check it when the family changes.

steps.prompt: Who is the beneficiary?
choices: The person you name to receive the money if you die
steps.explain: You choose them. If you do not, the policy’s default may not be who you think.

steps.prompt: Why does a new child change the life-insurance question?
choices: Someone now depends on your income
Term life becomes a savings account
The premium is no longer owed
steps.explain: The need is the dependent. The product is still term life, not a new kind of account.

steps.prompt: A term policy pays the beneficiary every year, like a paycheck, while you are alive.
steps.explain: It pays if you die during the term. It is not income while you are living.

steps.prompt: The person who receives the life insurance is the ___.
steps.explain: Name them, and update the name when life changes.

lessons.title: A Family Month
lessons.summary: Childcare gets the first claim. Then the rest of the $2,000.

steps.title: Two thousand dollars
steps.body:
This month has **$2,000** for the new family costs. Childcare needs at least **$1,200**. Diapers and food need at least **$200**.

What remains can go to a college jar. Assign every dollar.

steps.prompt: Assign $2,000. Childcare needs at least $1,200, and diapers and food need at least $200.
steps.explain: Childcare is at least $1,200, diapers and food at least $200, and all $2,000 is assigned.

steps.prompt: Childcare takes $1,200 and diapers take $200. How much is left of the $2,000?
That leftover $600 goes to the college jar every month. How much is that in a year?
The college jar should be filled before the childcare bill.
steps.explain: Care is due this month. The college jar is what is left after the bills that cannot wait.

lessons.title: Maria’s Twins
lessons.summary: Two credits are not two childcare bills paid.

story.title: Maria’s twins
story.body:
Maria is 34. She is having twins, and her income is **$85,000**, under the 2026 line where the [[child tax credit]] starts to shrink.

At the full amount, two qualifying children are **$2,200** × 2, which is **$4,400**. Childcare is **$1,000** a child each month, so **$2,000** a month, or **$24,000** a year.

Her plan offers the 2026 [[Dependent Care FSA|dependent-care-fsa]] limit of **$7,500**. That covers part of the childcare. It does not cover the year.

steps.prompt: At the full 2026 amount, what is the child tax credit for Maria’s two children?
steps.explain: $2,200 × 2 = $4,400. Her $85,000 income is under the $200,000 phaseout.

steps.prompt: Childcare is $1,000 per child per month. What is a month for both?
What is that childcare for a year?
The FSA covers $7,500. How much of the $24,000 is still outside it?
The $4,400 child tax credit pays the $24,000 childcare bill.
steps.explain: The credit is $4,400 at the full amount. Childcare is $24,000. They are not the same pile of money.

lessons.summary: Smart repetition on what you’re closest to forgetting.

lessons.title: Den Trial: Kids & Family Costs
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: Formula is $90 a month. What is the year?
A 2026 child tax credit at the full amount, for one qualifying child, is how much?
steps.explain: Up to $2,200, if income is under the phaseout.

steps.prompt: Which account is the 2026 work benefit for childcare, up to $7,500 if the plan offers it?
steps.explain: The FSA is for this year’s care. A 529 is for education later. Escrow pays tax and insurance.

steps.prompt: Once you have a child, term life insurance is a savings plan you can spend.
steps.explain: It pays a beneficiary if you die during the term.
